# Owned actual qualification prerequisite (not executed)

Use an isolated disposable PostgreSQL database with bootstrap, provisioning and migrations 1 through 26 in exact ledger order. Seed an enabled gateway-authorized source/collector and SQL26 gateway enrollment; separately seed an authorized producer runtime, current SQL19 session, SQL22 generation and SQL23 marker binding with its product credential/lifecycle/instance. Producer and gateway sources/collectors should differ. Ingest a committed V2 REQUEST through the existing origin-proof path with actual synthetic trusted issuer witness and materialize catalog observation and complete projection using the existing historical-origin qualification setup; preserve original immutable proof and exact tuple. Response and unattributed/missing/corrupt projection fixtures require independent cases. Keep every policy/session/gateway lease current through final checks.

In the same psql session, set tenant context and create `pg_temp.observer_seed(raw bytea NOT NULL, proof contour.verified_observer_claim NOT NULL)` with exactly one canonical observer JSON byte string and an issuer assertion whose observer peer leaf equals gateway enrollment, producer claim/epoch equals active SQL19, public key/generation equals SQL23, and root/activity/attempt/wire digest are the verified-marker claims. Use the explicit SQL marker-wire SHA256 domain. The seed must use synthetic data and is a trusted issuer assertion, not real Ed25519 or mTLS verification. Grant temporary seed SELECT to `contour_causal_observer_writer`, then run `db/tests/causal_observer_inbox.sql` in autocommit with ON_ERROR_STOP. The fixture errors if seed missing. This seed recipe is not yet an executable seed driver; materialization order and exact grants must be implemented/reviewed by the owned actual lane rather than bypassing integrity triggers or inserting fabricated proof/projection rows.

Run concurrent independent connections for cross-tenant same-attempt/delivery races, retry predecessor cycles, lock contention, stale-policy retries, per-insert quota rollback, ledger 1..26/1..27 and repeated migration guards. Real future server verification must prove mTLS, marker signatures, SQL25 original peer, and runtime origin binding. No source-shape or unit test establishes these facts.

The companion owned harness must derive the seed from the active (not revoked) SQL17 product proof and checked catalog tuple, and provision an independently authorized SQL18 runtime source and SQL26 gateway capture source. A committed attempt may be absent when the first observer is stored. The fixture subsequently checks a linked retry after quota recovery, a missing predecessor stored unresolved and a cycle-forming predecessor rejected; it must run within the original current policy/session/gateway leases. A separate valid seed with the same record UUID in another batch is needed to test attempt-to-batch conflict; simply changing a UUID to an uncommitted tuple tests absence, not that conflict.

Retry chains have a fail-closed capacity of 64 stored deliveries per connected chain. The SQL fixture uses psql `\gexec` with autocommit to construct two 31-node fragments and join them, accepts the 64th and rejects the 65th, then constructs two 32-node fragments and rejects a late parent joining both. These repeated full authority/proof checks require live original leases and may be slow; expiration must fail the test rather than extend a deadline. A separate concurrent driver must race two distinct children for the same known or missing predecessor in both arrival orders: exactly one commits, the other gets 23505 or 40001 and leaves no quota/fact; rerun only with fresh authorization. The partial unique index arbitrates even if application checks race.

A separate two-attempt synthetic issuer seed must race or sequentially submit children with the same `(tenant,gateway,generation,retry_of)` but different producer attempts, in each order, including when the parent is missing. At most one child can commit; verify the loser leaves no receipt, fact, attempt reservation, epoch reservation or quota delta. This requires independently valid signed-marker assertions and committed origin mapping for each attempt; do not reuse a proof object with a forged attempt merely to exercise the index. The SQL-only single-attempt fixture above does not establish this case.
